_comment_story_merge: The story-merge family -- cmd_story_merge, _story_merge_resolve_axis and the three writers -- captured the same way, before its jq was deleted: 92 cases over one adversarial corpus spanning legacy mode, both split axes, --foundation, --phase-aware, --agent-mode, and the write failures nobody had exercised. Recorded per case: the flags, the staging files it was handed (`input`, so the case is REPLAYABLE and not merely described), exit code, stdout, stderr, every file left under .aimi/tasks with its content, and the whole .aimi tree listing, so a refusal that wrote something as a side effect could not hide. Each case ran in its own throwaway project root; paths are relative because the flags were; createdAt normalizes to <DATE> (it is today's date by construction), mktemp's six random characters to <MKTEMP> (that one SURVIVED is the evidence, not which one), and the absolute script path and line number a shell diagnostic quotes to <CLI> and <N>. Two runs of the pre-port CLI produce this file byte for byte. 440 of 460 field comparisons identical after the port -- every stdout, stderr, written file and tree matched in 84 of the 92 cases, including every case the 41 black-box calls in the bash suite drive. The 20 that differ fall in 8 cases and are ALL of one kind: jq or `set -e` aborting before the code's own diagnostic could run, so the exit status was the engine's and the message the code was written to print was unreachable. They are named here so nobody has to rediscover them. (1) arquivo-array, the loud one: a staging file holding an ARRAY of stories, which the story-merge docs promise is supported. The bash has a complete flattening loop for it, introduced with the comment 'Simpler approach: just append with sequential indices' -- and directly above that loop a first attempt calling `path` with no argument, which is a compile error, whose 2>/dev/null'd failure assigned the EMPTY STRING over the accumulator the loop was about to append to. jq then aborted (exit 5, 'null (null) has no keys') and nothing was ever written. The Python runs the loop the bash was written to run, so an array file now merges. This is the one recorded difference that is a capability rather than a message, and it is deliberate: writing code to reproduce a swallowed compile error would be writing the defect on purpose. (2) json-numero and json-string (exit 5 -> 1): a staging file whose top-level value is a number or a string. jq aborted adding it to {_srcIdx}; the Python refuses by name and says which file. (3) json-multiplos-valores (exit 2 -> 1): two JSON values in one file. `jq -e .` accepted it and `--argjson` rejected it three steps later; the Python reports it at the malformed-JSON check, which is where that question was already being asked. (4) dep-nao-string (exit 5 -> 1): a dependsOn entry that is not a string. jq aborted in startswith(); the Python lets it through the outline remap, and Kahn's algorithm reports it as a cycle -- which is what the bash already did for every other dependsOn naming no story, and is preserved on purpose. (5) escrita-legada-falha and side-escrita-falha: a directory where the lock file goes. `set -e` killed the shell on the failing `200>` redirect, so the legacy and SIDE writers' own 'failed to write output file' branch was unreachable dead code and the mktemp scratch file survived. The Python prints that message and removes the scratch file. Both remain refusals at exit 1 that write no tasks file, which the file and tree fields confirm. (6) proj-falha-parcial: the same obstacle on the PROJECT axis, where `|| write_exit=$?` kept the branch reachable. Its whole three-set report is byte-identical; the only difference is the shell's own redirect diagnostic, which preceded it and has no Python equivalent.

_comment_tasks_read: The six read-only tasks.json verbs -- status (both branches), metadata, get-story, current-story, get-state and count-pending -- captured the same way, before their jq was deleted: 151 cases over one adversarial corpus, at commit 9716146. Recorded per case: the argv, the tasks file the run was given and the .aimi/state/ files it started with (`input`, so the case is REPLAYABLE and not merely described), exit code, stdout, stderr, and every .aimi/ file left behind afterwards (`state_after`), so a read-only verb that wrote something as a side effect could not hide -- 19 cases legitimately leave one, and those recordings are the evidence that get_tasks_file's stale-state self-heal and its .state.lock still run in bash. Each case ran in its own throwaway project root; exactly one normalization rule fired, the temp root to /TMP, and nothing else in the recording is non-deterministic: two runs of the pre-port CLI produce this file byte for byte. The corpus is weighted toward inputs the schema does not allow, because that is the only place jq and Python can differ -- the maxConcurrency value space on all three former call sites (absent, null, false, true, 0, 0.0, -1, -0.5, 20.0, 20.5, 999999, a string, an array, an object), metadata absent / null / {} / a string / an array / a number, userStories absent / null / [] / an object / a string across five verbs, a story that is null and a story that is a string, dependsOn null / false / a string, priority as 1.0, an unknown story id, a duplicated story id, a current-story pointer that is unset / empty / stale / never validated, no tasks file at all, a stale current-tasks pointer, the nested phase-folder layout, and seven whole-document shapes (malformed, empty, null, an array, a number, a string, two concatenated values). 530 of 604 field comparisons identical after the port -- every stdout and every state_after matched in all 151 cases, and 114 of the 151 matched on all four fields. Every clamp case is byte-identical on all three call sites, which is the thing this slice existed to prove: `true` still clamps to 20 because jq orders booleans below numbers so `true <= 0` holds, 0 and 0.0 still clamp because jq's `//` treats both as present, 20.0 still renders as 20 rather than 20.0, and a string, an array or an object still passes through UNCHANGED because jq orders those above numbers and the comparison is simply false -- the case a naive Python `value <= 0` raises TypeError on. The 74 fields that differ fall in 37 cases, are exit code and stderr only, and are ALL of one kind: jq aborting mid-expression, so the exit status was the engine's (5 for a runtime error, 4 for a parse error) and the message the code would otherwise have printed did not exist. Every one of them was, and still is, a refusal that writes nothing to stdout; only the wording and the number moved, to `Error: <verb>: <file>: <expression>: <what went wrong>` at exit 1. Recorded rather than reproduced: synthesizing an engine error would be the only way to match, and that is not a thing to write on purpose -- same shape as the nine named in _comment_lifecycle. They cluster into five classes, and KNOWN_DIVERGENCES in test_tasks.py names all 37 individually. (1) userStories absent, null, an object or a string: 16 cases across status, status --counts-only, count-pending and current-story (`status-us-*`, `counts-us-*`, `count-pending-us-*`, `current-story-us-*`), all of them jq's 'Cannot iterate over null' or 'Cannot iterate over string'. get-story is NOT among them -- validate_story_exists still runs in bash and refuses first, so all five of its us-* cases are byte-identical, which is what keeping that gate out of Python bought. (2) metadata a string, an array or a number: 4 cases (`meta-string`, `meta-array`, `meta-numero`, `status-meta-string`), jq's 'Cannot index ... with string'. (3) a whole document that is not an object: 13 cases (`doc-json-array-*`, `doc-json-numero-*`, `doc-json-string-*`, `doc-json-null-status`, `doc-json-null-count`, `doc-json-dois-valores-status`, `doc-json-dois-valores-count`). doc-json-null-METADATA is deliberately not among them: jq's assignment onto null BUILDS the object, so a null document still yields {"maxConcurrency": 20}, and the port does the same. (4) malformed JSON: 3 cases (`doc-json-malformado-*`), jq's own parse error at exit 4. (5) a story that is not an object: 1 case (`historia-nao-objeto`). A story that is NULL is deliberately not among them -- jq indexes null happily and emits a row of nulls, which the port reproduces. Two jq behaviours that have nothing to do with the tasks schema were preserved rather than tidied away, and both are byte-identical here. An EMPTY tasks file makes jq read zero values from its input stream, so the verb prints nothing and exits 0 (`doc-json-vazio-*`, 3 cases): a truncated write reports success, which is a silent hole, ranked and left alone because a port is not where a defect is fixed. And a file holding two concatenated documents runs the verb once per document (`doc-json-dois-valores-metadata`, which prints two objects). tasks.py's read_docs reads the same stream for both reasons; a plain json.load would have broken four otherwise-identical cases to no one's benefit.
